newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends mixed, Sept holds range.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends mixed, Sept holds range.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended mixed Monday in a moderate session, with September losing some ground but holding its recent technical range in the face of a firmer physical market, trade sources said.
September eased 0.6 cent to close at $2.426 per million British thermal units. October settled 1.9 cents lower at $2.445. Most others ended steady to up two cents.

"Cash held up and the board just couldn't come off a whole lot. If cash doesn't break this week with a cool front in Chicago and New York, you could see the shorts get very nervous (before September expires on Wednesday, August 27)," said one Midwest trader.

Despite fairly mild weather across northern tier states and forecasts for more of the same through the week, few expected prices to crater anytime soon, with stocks still lagging the three-year average by almost 10 percent.

Technical traders said September seemed range-bound, with support still pegged at Friday's low of $2.395 and then at $2.34 and $2.30. Better buying was expected in the $2.25-2.27 area. Resistance was seen at $2.55 and then at the contract high and double top at $2.605. Further selling was likely in the $2.64-2.655 spot continuation chart gap from late January.

In the cash Monday, Gulf Coast prices firmed three cents to the low-to-mid $2.50s. Midcon pipes were steady to up slightly in the low-to-mid $2.40s. New York city gate gas also was modestly higher in the mid-to-high $2.70s.
The NYMEX Henry Hub 12-month strip was unchanged at $2.353. NYMEX said 35,727 contracts traded, down from Friday's revised tally of 368.

On the KCBT, September finished 0.7 cent lower at $2.355, while deferreds ended steady to down 1.2 cents. The East/West spread widened by 0.1 cent to 7.1 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 390 lots traded, up from Friday's total of 300.
